Selected studies · Abstract-based

Weekly CPB & ECMO Research

A short selection of recently published studies. Each highlight reports only what the PubMed abstract says. Open the original record for details.

October 26 – November 1, 2026

  1. VA-ECMORandomized mechanistic trialOctober 31

    IABP and microaxial pumps during VA-ECMO

    HERACLES randomized 24 patients with cardiogenic shock on VA-ECMO to left ventricular unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or a microaxial flow pump.

    The abstract reports improved myocardial oxygen supply–demand balance with IABP but not the microaxial pump (ratio 1.48 vs 0.97; P=0.036). Thirty-day mortality was similar between groups.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42966011) →
  2. ECMOObservational cohortOctober 30

    ECMO use in infarction-related cardiogenic shock

    A study of 102,718 Medicare beneficiaries compared ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, and medical management for myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock.

    ECMO was used in 1,165 patients (1.1%). Adjusted analyses estimated 30-day mortality at 68–70% in the ECMO group; the authors state that their analyses could not establish a causal effect on survival.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42960751) →
  3. Pediatric ECPRRegistry studyOctober 29

    How much does pediatric ECPR survival vary by hospital?

    ELSO registry data from 1,377 children treated with ECPR after in-hospital cardiac arrest were used to develop and internally validate a survival model.

    The validation cohort had an area under the curve of 0.678. The authors found variation in risk-adjusted survival between hospitals and cautioned that the model is limited as a standalone clinical decision tool.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42951894) →
  4. ECPRRetrospective studyOctober 29

    Early lactate response after ECPR

    Researchers analyzed 91 patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated with ECPR, comparing lactate before support and 12 hours after ECMO initiation.

    At 12 hours, lactate was lower in survivors than nonsurvivors (5.45 vs 9.04 mmol/L; P=0.002). Lactate before reperfusion did not differ between those groups.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42956360) →
  5. Cardiac surgery · CPBRandomized trialOctober 30

    Stellate ganglion block and postoperative atrial fibrillation

    In a single-center trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with CPB were randomized to preoperative stellate ganglion block or saline; 132 were analyzed.

    Postoperative atrial fibrillation occurred in 43% and 40% of patients, respectively (adjusted P=0.989). The trial did not show a reduction in its primary outcome.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42960736) →

October 19–25, 2026

Show studies ↓Hide studies ↑
  1. ECPRNationwide observational studyOctober 25

    Does ECPR timing affect outcomes after cardiac arrest?

    A nationwide analysis followed 58,668 people with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest; 909 received ECPR. It compared patients still in refractory arrest at the same decision times.

    The abstract reports an association between ECPR and better 30-day survival and neurological outcomes at each time point, including after 60 minutes. The observational design cannot establish that ECPR caused the difference.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42926135) →
  2. ECMO · Lung transplantRetrospective cohortOctober 21

    Age and outcomes after ECMO bridging to lung transplant

    A single-center cohort included 115 adults listed for lung transplantation while on ECMO; 93 underwent transplantation. The researchers compared recipients younger than 50 with those aged 50 or older.

    Five-year graft survival was 77% in the younger group and 44% in the older group. Age 50 or older was associated with higher adjusted graft-loss risk, but this study cannot define an age cutoff for individual patients.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42906575) →
  3. VA-ECMO · CannulationRetrospective cohortOctober 21

    Axillary versus femoral arterial cannulation after heart transplant

    In 42 heart transplant recipients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for primary graft dysfunction, 17 had axillary Dacron-graft cannulation and 25 had direct femoral cannulation.

    Cannulation-related complications occurred in 0 of 17 and 3 of 25 patients, respectively. The difference was not statistically significant; neither were differences in ECMO weaning or survival to discharge.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42940214) →
  4. Aortic surgery · CPBRetrospective studyOctober 22

    Hypothermia level during emergency aortic surgery

    A single-center study compared temperature strategies in 175 emergency operations for acute aortic syndrome; most patients underwent hemiarch repair.

    In the hemiarch subgroup, warmer temperatures were associated with less stroke and shorter intensive care stays. The four-category comparison did not remain significant after adjustment; a separate analysis using 24°C as the cutoff found lower adjusted stroke risk above 24°C.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42911832) →
  5. Extracorporeal circulationRetrospective imaging studyOctober 20

    Cerebral microbleeds after surgery with extracorporeal circulation

    Researchers reviewed brain MRI scans in 111 people with heritable connective tissue disorders and compared cerebral microbleeds with their surgical histories.

    All 58 patients exposed to surgery with extracorporeal circulation had microbleeds, compared with four people who had not undergone surgery. Microbleed burden increased with repeat procedures and longer extracorporeal circulation exposure; the study did not measure clinical neurological outcomes.

    Read the PubMed record (PMID 42899414) →

Selected for relevance to CPB and ECMO practice, not as a complete list of each week's publications. These summaries are based on abstracts and are for education; they are not treatment recommendations.
